fixes.where: Notes panel, 'Build notes for the live release': a new note 8 after 'Events for the test' (prototype.html L607). Script L634-636: the pixel comment and var ARM.
fixes.change:
Add the test harness. Without it, the comment at L634 ('the live test can be read from Shopify orders by arm') has nothing behind it. New note 8, verbatim:
'The test harness. Arm: computed once per visitor from naira_vid (visitorId.ts): the first 8 hex digits of its SHA-256, mod 2 (0 = pdp_a, 1 = pdp_b). It is decided before JewelDetail renders, on every jewellery PDP, so a returning visitor never switches arms. Mobile only; desktop stays on arm A and is left out of the read.
Orders: add { key: "nf_arm", value: arm } to trackingCartAttributes() in src/lib/shopify.ts and to fastrrCartAttributes() in src/lib/fastrr.ts. naira_visitor_id already travels in both.
Before launch, ops places one Fastrr test order and reads order.customAttributes. If nf_arm and naira_visitor_id are there, orders are read by arm from Shopify. If Fastrr drops them, meta-capi (which already receives InitiateCheckout and Purchase with an event_id) writes {event_id, naira_vid, arm, value, num_items} to a Supabase table, and orders are joined on the Purchase event.
Freeze promo.ts and BUY2/BUY3/BUY4 for the whole test.
Read per visitor, never per event: visitors who added / PDP visitors, visitors who began checkout / visitors who added, Shopify orders / PDP visitors. Pixel Purchase is never the decision metric.'
In the script: change L634's comment to end '...read from Shopify orders by arm (build note 8)', and set var ARM = window.__nfArm || 'pdp_b'; so the live build sets the arm in one place.
fixes.why:
Test validity, which is the proof this page has to earn. Naira data [N]:
- Pixel Purchase runs at 692 events against about 204 orders (3.4x).
- Meta attributes 243 purchases against 206 orders.
So orders by arm must come from Shopify.
Arm B moves ATC and IC per event mechanically:
- It has four add surfaces beyond the bar (the card's + Add, set rows, Add all, the bag's + Add), so ATC events per adding visitor rise and IC/ATC per event falls.
- Buy now fires ATC and IC together.
- The bag's COD line moves some COD drop-off from Fastrr to before IC.
IC/ATC per event is therefore the one ratio that cannot decide this test. The plumbing already exists: shopify.ts L464-473 and fastrr.ts cartAttributes already carry naira_visitor_id, fbc and fbp, so this is one key plus one verification order.

roadmap: Owner, launch blocker 4: Buy now and the COD fee. Buy now is the only route to Fastrr with no rupee COD figure on our pages. Pick wording (a) or (b) from the notes before launch.
Owner: confirm the prepaid 5% (55 of ~105 prepaid orders carried it). Then the bag foot reads 'Pay online ₹2,279 · COD ₹2,519 (₹120 fee)' at equal weight, and Buy now can carry the online price.

Pre-launch comprehension check on the ladder, about a day's work. Show fold.png to 15-20 Instagram shoppers (the Inner Circle list or WhatsApp) and ask: 'What would this bracelet and the ring cost together?' If more than 1 in 5 answer ₹2,159, the bundle reading is real. Then test the caption 'Mix any pieces, no code · this bracelet then costs' before launch.
Reviews (C4): a review app requesting reviews 7 days after delivery, with photo reviews. Show a rating and count beside the H1 only from 5 real reviews [S16].
Ad map (C17): every live ad's utm_content in a <piece>_<asset>_<angle> convention, with the ads owner's own promise per angle.

TEST 1, the new template against the honest arm A (build note 1), mobile only, on every jewellery PDP; Prism alone sells about 10 a month.
- Traffic: about 8,000 mobile PDP views a week from the browser pixel, about 4,000 per arm.
- ATC per visitor from ~15.8%: +12% relative needs ~6,050 per arm (1.5 weeks).
- IC per visitor from ~3.0%: +20% needs ~13,900 per arm (3.5 weeks).
- Orders per visitor (~0.87%): +20% needs ~49,000 per arm (12 weeks). Report it as probability-to-beat after at least 4 weeks (two weekly cycles and a month-start payday).
- Expect: ATC/visitor +10 to +20%; IC per adding visitor −5% to +5% (one more tap, and the COD figure before IC); orders/IC +5 to +15%; items per order 1.51 → 1.6-1.7; COD share −3 to −6 points.
- Guardrails: orders/IC on Android (16.6% today against 27.9% on iPhone), cancellations, RTO matured at 3 weeks.
- All rates per visitor, through fix 1.

TEST 2, the post-add step inside arm B on the new bag: card + 'Bag & checkout' against an auto-opened bag that carries the 'Wear it with' row (one tap shorter, as live). Primary: orders per adding visitor. Diagnostics: nf_bag_view, nf_card_add against nf_drawer_add, and the nf_card_shown mode mix (after fixes 2 and 4, full/compact/slim should cover most adds above the set).

TEST 3: the price-row slot ('Surgical steel, PVD rhodium' against 'Waterproof · tarnish free', with a third arm 'Arrives gift-boxed' through the Nov-Feb gifting season). TEST 4: Buy now as the ink primary against Add to bag (68-74% of orders are one piece). Guardrails: COD share and RTO.

TEST 5, once nf_contact has two weeks of data. Reassurance list with 'Faulty piece?' first and 'Questions' last, and @naira.flore as plain text when the user agent contains 'Instagram' (the profile link leaves the in-app browser). Keep WhatsApp a link. TEST 6, low priority: the empty 'Reviews' section against no section until reviews exist. Primary for both: ATC per visitor.
RUM inside the Instagram webview: field LCP, the nf_tap_guarded rate by control (above ~2% of adds means real double taps are common), and nf_bag_exit by device and by bag size.
